note: English copy for /en/bots/. Facts follow the official docs linked in data/ai-crawlers.json (verified_on there). Keep in sync when that file changes.

GPTBot.summary: OpenAI's training crawler. It collects public pages that may be used to train OpenAI's generative foundation models.
GPTBot.block: Your content is excluded from training OpenAI's foundation models. It does not affect whether you appear in ChatGPT search; that is OAI-SearchBot.
GPTBot.advice: Block it if you don't want your content used for training. Blocking it alone won't remove you from ChatGPT answers.

OAI-SearchBot.summary: OpenAI's search crawler. It surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features and is independent of GPTBot.
OAI-SearchBot.block: Your site won't be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though it can still appear as a navigational link.
OAI-SearchBot.advice: Allow it if you want ChatGPT to cite and link your pages. This is the crawler most worth unblocking at the firewall.

ChatGPT-User.summary: Fetches made when a ChatGPT or Custom GPT user asks it to visit a page. It is not an automatic crawler.
ChatGPT-User.block: OpenAI says robots.txt rules may not apply to user-initiated fetches. It doesn't decide whether you appear in ChatGPT search.
ChatGPT-User.advice: Leave it allowed unless you have a specific reason. A firewall block stops ChatGPT from reading a page a user pasted in.

ClaudeBot.summary: Anthropic's training crawler. It collects public web content that may be used to train Claude models.
ClaudeBot.block: Your site's future content is excluded from Anthropic's model training datasets.
ClaudeBot.advice: Block it to opt out of Anthropic training. Claude's search and user fetches use separate agents.

Claude-SearchBot.summary: Anthropic's search crawler. It indexes content to improve the quality of Claude's search results.
Claude-SearchBot.block: Claude won't index your content for search, which may reduce your visibility and accuracy in Claude's answers.
Claude-SearchBot.advice: Allow it if you want to be found and cited in Claude search.

Claude-User.summary: Fetches made when a Claude user asks a question that needs your page.
Claude-User.block: Claude can't retrieve your content in response to user queries, which may reduce your visibility for user-directed search.
Claude-User.advice: Leave it allowed if you want Claude to read your pages when users ask about them.

Google-Extended.summary: A robots.txt product token, not a separate crawler. Googlebot does the fetching; Google-Extended controls whether that content may be used for Gemini training and grounding.
Google-Extended.block: Your content isn't used to train future Gemini models and isn't used for grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. Google Search is unaffected.
Google-Extended.advice: Disallow Google-Extended, never Googlebot, if you want to opt out of Gemini training. Note that it also removes you from Gemini Apps grounding.

Googlebot.summary: Google's main search crawler. Rules for Googlebot apply to Google Search, Discover and other Google Search features.
Googlebot.block: Your site drops out of Google Search, including AI Overviews. This is almost never what you want when opting out of AI.
Googlebot.advice: Keep it allowed. To opt out of Gemini training, disallow Google-Extended instead.

Applebot.summary: Apple's search crawler for Spotlight, Siri and Safari features. If robots.txt doesn't mention Applebot but mentions Googlebot, Applebot follows the Googlebot rules.
Applebot.block: Your site won't appear in Apple's search features such as Spotlight, Siri and Safari suggestions.
Applebot.advice: Keep it allowed. To opt out of Apple's AI training, disallow Applebot-Extended.

Applebot-Extended.summary: A robots.txt token, not a crawler. It controls whether content Applebot collected may be used to train Apple's foundation models.
Applebot-Extended.block: Your content isn't used to train the models behind Apple Intelligence. Pages that disallow it can still appear in Apple search results.
Applebot-Extended.advice: Disallow it to opt out of Apple training without leaving Apple search.

PerplexityBot.summary: Perplexity's search crawler. It surfaces and links websites in Perplexity search results and is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models.
PerplexityBot.block: Your site won't be surfaced or linked in Perplexity search results.
PerplexityBot.advice: Allow it if you want Perplexity to cite you. Blocking it doesn't opt you out of any training.

Perplexity-User.summary: Fetches made when a Perplexity user asks a question that needs your page.
Perplexity-User.block: Perplexity says this fetcher generally ignores robots.txt because a user requested it. Only a firewall rule actually stops it.
Perplexity-User.advice: Leave it allowed unless you have a reason to block user-directed fetches.

Bingbot.summary: Microsoft's standard search crawler. Bing's index also feeds Microsoft Copilot and other AI experiences built on Bing.
Bingbot.block: Your site drops out of Bing search and the AI experiences that rely on Bing's index.
Bingbot.advice: Keep it allowed. Bing's training opt-out today is the NOARCHIVE meta tag; Microsoft is building support for a robots.txt no-training preference, targeted for early 2027.

CCBot.summary: Common Crawl's crawler. It builds an open web dataset that many AI models have been trained on.
CCBot.block: Future pages won't enter the Common Crawl dataset. Snapshots already published are not withdrawn.
CCBot.advice: Block it if you don't want your pages in open training datasets. It has no effect on any search engine.

Bytespider.summary: ByteDance's crawler, documented as the user agent for Toutiao search.
Bytespider.block: Your site may drop out of Toutiao search. ByteDance doesn't document whether blocking it stops AI training use.
Bytespider.advice: Block it if you don't need Toutiao traffic. Its training use is undocumented.

PetalBot.summary: Huawei's crawler for Petal Search. Huawei says its index also powers Huawei Assistant and AI Search, and that it follows robots.txt.
PetalBot.block: Your site drops out of Petal Search, and Huawei Assistant and AI Search lose your content. Huawei doesn't say whether it's used for model training.
PetalBot.advice: Keep it if you want traffic from Huawei phones and Petal Search.

meta-externalagent.summary: Meta's crawler for use cases such as training foundation AI models or improving products by indexing content directly.
meta-externalagent.block: Meta-ExternalAgent stops fetching your content, including for training Meta's foundation models.
meta-externalagent.advice: Block it to opt out of Meta AI training.

meta-webindexer.summary: Meta's indexing crawler. Meta says allowing it helps Meta AI cite and link your content in its responses.
meta-webindexer.block: Meta AI may stop citing and linking your content in its answers.
meta-webindexer.advice: Allow it if you want to be cited in Meta AI.

meta-externalfetcher.summary: Fetches requested by Meta AI users, for example when a user shares a link.
meta-externalfetcher.block: Meta says this fetcher may bypass robots.txt because the fetch was requested by a user. Only a firewall rule actually stops it.
meta-externalfetcher.advice: Leave it allowed unless you have a reason to block user-directed fetches.

Amazonbot.summary: Amazon's crawler, used to improve Amazon products and services. Amazon says the content may be used to train Amazon AI models.
Amazonbot.block: Amazonbot stops fetching your content, including for possible AI training. Alexa search is controlled separately by Amzn-SearchBot.
Amazonbot.advice: Block it to opt out of Amazon training while keeping Amzn-SearchBot allowed.

Amzn-SearchBot.summary: Amazon's search crawler for experiences such as Alexa. Amazon says it doesn't crawl content for generative AI model training.
Amzn-SearchBot.block: Your content can't appear in Amazon search experiences such as Alexa.
Amzn-SearchBot.advice: Allow it if you want to be found through Alexa and Amazon search.

DuckAssistBot.summary: DuckDuckGo's crawler for its AI-assisted answers. It fetches pages in real time and DuckDuckGo says the data isn't used to train AI models.
DuckAssistBot.block: Your pages stop being a source for DuckDuckGo's AI-assisted answers. Regular DuckDuckGo rankings are unaffected.
DuckAssistBot.advice: Allow it if you want to be cited in DuckDuckGo's AI answers.

Baiduspider.summary: Baidu's search crawler. It follows robots.txt.
Baiduspider.block: Your pages can't be found on Baidu or on any search engine that uses Baidu's search service.
Baiduspider.advice: Keep it allowed if you want traffic from China.
